answer: The shared physical-slot registration mechanism gives each agent identity a distinct monitored occupancy slot for a fixed shift at a verified site, such as a specific mesa in a partner workspace. The registry enforces one live identity per slot and requires a fresh signed occupancy proof for handoff, so a reused jetty checkpoint reading or duplicated beacon collapses the claim to one identity. To create N identities an attacker must staff N separate slots through the full window, paying idle labor, travel, and coordination, plus a forfeited opal-marked deposit tag for each failed check.
